summary: Three measured rounds took selu_ from 0.7527x to 0.8871x geo_mean against the PyTorch reference, with all 36 workloads passing. The winning architecture combines a bare-integer-address host fast path that calls the compiled launcher from a single frame (nine launch-bound cases 18.5us -> 12.8us) with a persistent grid-stride kernel at one program per queried vector core for long contiguous tensors (fp16 16M 1.25x -> 1.36x, bf16 0.71x -> 0.78x, fp32 0.60x -> 0.68x). The key lesson from on-target probes is that the large cases were bound by per-program tile overhead, not by exp arithmetic (a same-tile copy cost 78us of 83us, and exp2/fp16-negative variants were slower or UB-infeasible), while the small cases were bound by host Python, not by the 9.4us compiled launch floor.
